ircc.name: FutureCanada (IRCC capstone)
ircc.title: FutureCanada (IRCC capstone)
ircc.summary: Per-province forecasts of immigration’s impact on Canadian housing and education capacity out to 2035, built with IRCC as the capstone partner. Sree was the lead contributor in a five-person team and led the data engineering and modelling.
ircc.problem: Demand for housing and school capacity depends on permanent and temporary resident admissions, and the relationship differs by province.
architecture: Open Canada, CMHC and Statistics Canada data
ircc.decision: Prophet with exogenous regressors, RandomForest and XGBoost were compared per province on a chronological 80/20 holdout and selected by RMSE. Prophet won 8 of 9 regions (Ontario R² 0.965). A pooled model had made RandomForest look strong at R² 0.84; fitted per province it lost in every region, so pooling was dropped.
ircc.evidence: Holdout metrics per province and per model, and a star-schema Power BI model with DAX measures and what-if parameters for permanent and temporary resident levels. The case study on this site gives the full results.
ircc.limits: Team capstone, January to April 2025, not government employment. Three provinces have negative holdout R² under Prophet, lag features were computed without grouping by province, and the education forecasts have no holdout. The pipeline runs end to end but offline; it is not a production system.

bogdai.name: BogdAI contract risk review
bogdai.title: BogdAI contract risk review
bogdai.summary: A six-agent pipeline that reviews a contract and returns a typed risk report in which every finding cites its source clause. It was a team entry in the Microsoft Agents League Hackathon 2026, run on synthetic healthcare and pharma contracts.
bogdai.problem: A risk label is only useful if a reviewer can trace it back to the clause and the policy behind it.
bogdai.decision: A deterministic 7-rule engine decides which flags exist. The LLM only enriches each flag in JSON mode, and degrades per call to the rule output on failure, so the pipeline runs end to end with no cloud credentials. The report is validated against 9 Pydantic models, frozen as the contract for a teammate’s interface.
bogdai.evidence: A verifier agent checks every finding for a citation and evidence, forces human review on high-risk flags and scans for unsafe-advice phrasing. 45 tests: 44 pass and 1 is an expected failure. The design doc on this site lists the decisions and the rejected alternatives.
bogdai.limits: Synthetic contracts and policies only, no evaluation of LLM output, no prompt-injection testing, and recall bounded by the seven rules. Sree wrote the backend: the orchestrator, the six agents, the rule engine and 41 of the 45 tests. A teammate built the API and interface. It is not a validated compliance product.

whatsapp.name: WhatsApp agent for event promoters
whatsapp.title: WhatsApp agent for event promoters
whatsapp.summary: A production conversational agent on WhatsApp for EventLinx. Promoters create events, configure ticketing and query sales in English and French. Sree built the agent, with tool calling and memory, and the 45-tool MCP server in TypeScript that connects it to the company’s PostgreSQL database.
whatsapp.problem: An agent with write access to a production database must not invent values or commit a change the user did not approve.
whatsapp.decision: Human-in-the-loop by construction: every database write blocks on an explicit user confirmation that is enforced in code, outside the model. Worst-case reply time fell by about 70%, from 15–30 seconds to 4–9 seconds. The model was chosen by measurement: gpt-4.1-mini was kept after an A/B run against gpt-5.4-nano, 35 of 36 eval cases passing against 25.
whatsapp.evidence: Every release is gated by LLM-judged test conversations, a 550-case red-team suite and 2,000+ automated tests in CI.
whatsapp.limits: Client work at Lambton College × EventLinx. The code is private, so no repository is linked and no further detail about the system is published.

seating.name: Seating-chart detection
seating.title: Seating-chart detection
seating.summary: A vision service for EventLinx that converts an image of a venue’s seating chart into a structured, machine-readable seat map.
seating.problem: Seating charts arrive as images in many styles, and a seat map is only usable if the seat count is right.
seating.decision: Sree trained and fine-tuned YOLO11 and a custom ResNet18 CNN on GPUs with real and synthetic seat maps, benchmarked against 250+ real venue maps. He then replaced the trained pipeline with a single Azure OpenAI vision service once it measured better. Two designs were rejected on the evidence: a single-call design put 1 of 6 charts in range, and a cheaper tile model 0 of 7 against 5 of 7.
seating.evidence: The service hit expected seat counts on all 5 benchmark venues at a median cost of $0.91 per map.
seating.limits: Client work at Lambton College × EventLinx. The code is private, so no repository is linked and no further detail about the system is published.

hasten.name: Hasten
hasten.title: Hasten
hasten.summary: A local-first mobile app. A thought is captured by voice or text, and an on-device pipeline classifies, ranks and schedules it with no network call. Sree is the sole developer.
hasten.problem: Capture has to work with no account, no network path and no manual filing.
hasten.decision: React Native on Expo with on-device speech recognition in 6 locales and a rule-based NLP engine for segmentation and entity, date and urgency extraction. The classifier combines weighted rules, prototype similarity and feedback from user corrections, with feedback capped per token and confidence clamped to a fixed band. Three architectures were built and removed first: a Gemini cloud parser, a Flutter rewrite and a self-hosted Phi-3 server.
hasten.evidence: 325 Jest tests and 16 Maestro device flows, including accessibility regression and seeded 5,000-item stress runs, validated on a physical device. Category accuracy rose from 50.85% to 77.58% after tuning; that figure is self-reported and the eval tooling was later removed.
hasten.limits: Personal project, built with Claude Code. The current repository has no evals and runs no tests in CI. The postmortem on this site covers what was removed and why the record is incomplete.

governed-ai.name: Governed AI Reliability
governed-ai.title: Policy boundaries, reproducible evidence, durable workflows.
governed-ai.summary: An anonymized case-study draft about policy constraints, escalation behavior, reproducible defect investigation, and durable workflow design. Personal contributions require owner review.
governed-ai.problem: An AI workflow can produce a plausible answer while crossing a policy boundary, losing an escalation, or repeating a defect. Reliability requires explicit decisions, inspectable evidence, and a workflow that survives handoffs.
governed-ai.decision: Describe permitted actions and stop conditions before execution. Keep prohibited actions blocked; send ambiguous or insufficiently supported cases to a human reviewer with the reason and minimum necessary context. Preserve a reproducible investigation and an explicit resume condition.
governed-ai.policy: Illustrative design: encode action scope, required evidence, and approval conditions as testable constraints. Distinguish permitted actions, prohibited actions, and decisions that require review. An escalation does not itself grant permission.
governed-ai.escalation: Illustrative design: pause the affected action, record the trigger, and assign a reviewer with expected versus observed behavior and a clear decision request. Missing acknowledgement remains pending. Resume only after a recorded decision and a fresh policy check; retries must not bypass the gate.
governed-ai.investigation: Illustrative investigation: an ambiguous request should pause for review, but a retry proceeds without a decision. Reproduce with synthetic inputs, fixed preconditions, configuration and policy versions, exact steps, and a sanitized trace. Repeat runs to record variability; distinguish observations from hypotheses. Minimize the failing case, isolate one variable at a time, and test the proposed fix against both the failure and allowed behavior.
governed-ai.workflow: Illustrative design: maintain a versioned playbook with entry criteria, decision rules, ownership, evidence requirements, and closure criteria. Save the pending decision and completion state across handoffs or interruptions. Make retries safe to repeat, prevent duplicate side effects, and turn each confirmed defect into a regression scenario.
contributions: Review required — proposed personal contribution: I translated policy requirements into explicit constraints and boundary scenarios.
Review required — proposed personal contribution: I investigated escalation behavior and clarified when a workflow must pause, hand off, and resume.
Review required — proposed personal contribution: I built reproducible defect reports using minimal examples, expected versus observed behavior, and regression checks.
Review required — proposed personal contribution: I designed durable workflow guidance that preserves decisions, evidence, and ownership across handoffs.
governed-ai.evidence: Drafted from the owner's requested themes. The design and defect example are illustrative abstractions, not published incident records or verified implementation evidence. No private logs, screenshots, source links, or identifying details are included.
governed-ai.outcome: Intended value: a reviewer can understand why an action paused, another investigator can rerun a defect, and a later maintainer can continue the workflow. No measured reliability improvement, deployment status, or business outcome is claimed.
governed-ai.limits: Owner review required: confirm or revise each personal-contribution statement, distinguish individual work from team work, and confirm which illustrative practices reflect completed work. Scope, artifacts, and outcomes have not been independently verified.
